title: SDK Concierge Crash Course — Sprint Log
content:
Purpose
This is a working sprint-log draft for a 1-day "concierge" crash course we run for new integrator engineers and internal advocates. Goal: get an engineer from zero -> instrumented prototype calling Redwood SDKs with telemetry and a simple prompt-validation suite in under 3 hours, with a curated 60-minute demo for PMs/stakeholders. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: short checklists, friction paths, and probes to validate that the onboarding experience actually produces stable, observable integrations.

Audience
- Developer advocates and solutions engineers running the concierge session
- New integrator engineers and partner devs who need to ship an LLM-powered feature quickly
- Internal product/PMs who want a demoable artifact at the end of the session

High-level success criteria (for a single session)
- Prototype accepts input, triggers Redwood API (hosted or dedicated), and renders streamed output within 2 minutes of first code run.
- Basic telemetry present: request id, latency, model/version, token counts, and one custom business metric (e.g., queries_with_user_id).
- Prompt-validation harness with 5 golden examples passing (sanity) and at least 1 failing example flagged (quality check).
- CI gate created that runs the 5 prompt tests on PRs (flake tolerant).

Sprint timeline (recommended 3-hour concierge block + optional 1-hour stakeholder demo)
- 0:00–0:10 — Kickoff: context, success criteria, account/dns access check, API key provisioning walkthrough.
- 0:10–0:25 — Local dev setup: repo clone, env vars, example app scaffold (Node/Go/Python options).
- 0:25–0:45 — Wire a minimal SDK call: simple generation endpoint, parse response, display. Validate streaming if requested.
- 0:45–1:15 — Add telemetry: attach request id, instrument latency timers, propagate user_id and route tags. Hook to lightweight log sink (stdout -> integration to datadog/local).
- 1:15–1:45 — Prompt-validation lab: write 5 golden prompts, assert expected outputs (fuzzy match), create test runner script.
- 1:45–2:10 — Create CI job (GitHub Actions template) to run prompt tests on PRs and to fail only on regressions beyond tolerance.
- 2:10–2:40 — Smoke-tests and failure modes: simulate rate limit, model fallback, and network timeout. Document remediation steps.
- 2:40–3:00 — Polish + deploy demo branch and prepare 60-minute stakeholder walkthrough artifact.

Concierge checklist (pre-session)
- Ensure attendee has GitHub access and a sandbox org or repo fork ready.
- Provision API key with minimal quota and revoke token checklist.
- Spawn short-lived telemetry sink (local file or ephemeral datadog stream) and share read-only link.
- Prepare language-specific starter zips (node/py/go) and a one-command run script (./start.sh).

Minimal starter flow (step-by-step summary)
1) Clone starter repo and create .env from .env.example (INSERT API_KEY).
2) npm/pip/go mod install, then run: ./start.sh -> service runs on localhost:3000.
3) Open /playground route, enter prompt, click submit. Observe network call and streaming UI.
4) Check logs for request-id header and latency metrics.
5) Edit prompt validators file (prompts/test_cases.json) with 5 golden examples and expected canonical text or regex. Run `npm run prompt-test`.
6) Open PR with one commit that updates prompt set and adds the GitHub action from .github/workflows/prompt-tests.yml.

Telemetry probes and minimal schema
- Required fields per call: request_id, timestamp, elapsed_ms, model, model_version, token_in, token_out, route, env (sandbox/prod), user_id (if available).
- Lightweight logs for session: LEVEL | ts | request_id | msg | latency_ms | tokens_out | model.
- Post-session telemetry sanity checks: median latency < 350ms (token turn partials ignored), 95th percentile < 1200ms for echo tests, token counts within expected bound.

Prompt-validation lab — heuristic rules
- Use canonicalization: trim whitespace, normalize punctuation, lower-case for label comparisons where safe.
- For generation tests allow fuzzy matching: Jaro-Winkler threshold or token overlap > 0.7.
- Capture stochastic failures by running each test 3x and marking as flaky if results vary; track flakes in test metadata.

CI gating & deployment notes
- PR checks: prompt-tests (nonblocking for flaky failures with metadata), lint, unit smoke.
- Optional: deploy demo branch to ephemeral preview environment via simple Netlify/Vercel workflow. Keep secrets in environment per-branch.

Top failure patterns and immediate remediation (cheat sheet)
- No response / timeouts: check API key validity, region mismatch, and observe last-known connection ID. Retry with exponential backoff and add fallback to smaller model.
- High latency: check for large context token counts, disable verbose logging in production, enable prefix KV cache where available.
- Wrong persona/format: tighten prompt anchors, add system message enforcement, or apply structured output schema and validate server-side.

Session artifacts to hand off
- Demo branch URL + ephemeral deploy URL (if used).
- prompts/test_cases.json and prompt-test runner log.
- short telem-export.json (first 200 calls) and a one-page summary with highlighted issues.
- PR with CI job and run-book note (what to revert if keys leak).

Open questions / followups
- Should the concierge kit include a tiny local simulator for model fallbacks (to test canary policies without burning calls)?
- Add per-language curated presets that wire the same telemetry hooks idiomatically (Go logger adapter, Python struct logger, Node pino plugin). Priority: Node + Python.
- UX: add an in-repo README template that turns into a single-slide demo for stakeholders.

Next steps (owner assignments)
- Jordan: finalize starter zips and short-run script (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Aisha: author the prompt-validation runner and fuzzy-matching util (ETA 2026-03-23).
- Diego: GitHub Action templates and ephemeral deploy recipe (ETA 2026-03-30).

Notes to self
- Keep this lightweight — friction kills the concierge flow. For first-run, prefer one opinionated path rather than offering every language. Expand to polyglot after the flow stabilizes.
- Capture participant feedback in a one-click survey integrated into the demo branch UI.
